text: When starting a new project, setting clear goals is essential for success. A useful method is to create SMART goals, which are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you could state "increase page speed by 20% within three months." Once your goals are defined, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should have a clear deliverable, such as a completed report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by discussing these goals with everyone involved early on. This prevents misunderstandings and makes sure all team members and clients share the same vision and expectations.
